# privacy-flow

> Deterministic, offline static analysis of where personal data goes: logs, third-party SDKs, LLM providers and outbound HTTP. Cited file:line flow paths, SARIF, canonical JSON and Fides egress.

The command-line tool is `piiflow`; the package is `privacy-flow` everywhere (the names `pflow` on crates.io and PyPI belong to unrelated tools). It analyses TypeScript, JavaScript and Python with tree-sitter, follows calls across files and packages through function summaries, and reports each flow of personal data (Fideslang categories) to a sink as a chain of file:line:column hops. Anything it cannot see is reported as a coverage gap, and a result with open gaps never exits as clean. It makes no network calls, sends no telemetry and calls no model. MIT licensed, maintained by Noru (https://noru.tech).

Install:

```bash
brew install noru-tech/tap/piiflow         # Homebrew, macOS and Linux
cargo binstall privacy-flow                # prebuilt binary from GitHub Releases
cargo install privacy-flow --locked        # build from crates.io
```

Use:

```bash
piiflow scan .                             # writes .privacy-flow/flows.json; exit 4 if coverage is incomplete
piiflow explain pf-<id>                    # the hop chain, with the source line of each hop
piiflow check .privacy-flow/flows.json --as-of 2026-10-01    # exit 1 above the policy threshold
piiflow diff origin/main..HEAD -f sarif -o pr.sarif          # only flows a change introduces
```
